landing.faqRefundsQ: What changed in how refunds are counted?
landing.faqRefundsA: A refund used to count as lost revenue, and stock recovered from a return was ignored. Now a refund lowers net sales, recovered cost comes off product cost, the payment fee is its own line, and a refund dated after the period end is shown as a separate adjustment.
landing.trustTitle: AI that explains. An engine that counts. Your data stays yours.
landing.trustQuote: ChatGPT gives you a story once; Profyn gives you a ledger every month.
landing.trustWhy1: Every rupee comes from a tested engine with 360+ automated tests; the AI only explains the numbers.
landing.trustWhy2: Any AI sentence with a figure the engine did not produce is rejected before you see it.
landing.trustWhy3: Thousands of orders reconcile to channel and product totals, the same way every month.
landing.trustWhy4: Each decision is saved with the numbers it was based on and a 30-day check.
landing.trustPromise1: Stored in India on AWS Mumbai; uploaded files are encrypted at rest and every connection uses HTTPS.
landing.trustPromise2: Your account only: other accounts cannot read your data, and we never sell it.
landing.trustPromise3: The AI sees totals by cause, never your order rows, and it is off for your uploads unless you switch it on.
landing.trustPromise4: Export or delete everything at any time.

landing.heroEyebrow: AI profit analyst for D2C brands
landing.heroLead: Know where your money goes. Know what to do next.
landing.heroBody: Upload your order exports. {{brand}}'s AI works through every order — refunds, returns, shipping, fees and ads — finds where profit leaks, ranks the three fixes worth the most, and saves your decision in one click. Every rupee comes from a tested engine, never guessed.
landing.tickEngine: Every rupee from a tested engine
landing.featAutopilotText: Contribution per order, leaks by cause, and the top 3 fixes ranked in rupees, each explained in plain words and saved as a decision in one click.
landing.featAskText: Type or speak in English, Hindi or Telugu: "Which product lost most in September?" The answer comes from your own orders, with a link to the orders behind it.
landing.featLedgerTitle: Click a leak, see the orders
landing.featLedgerText: Every cause and chart opens the exact orders behind it. Totals reconcile across channels and products, and a missing value stays unknown, never zero.
landing.step1Text: Drop up to 12 CSV or JSON files at once. Every row is checked, and orders already saved are skipped.
landing.step2Title: AI finds the leaks and the fixes
landing.step2Text: Autopilot computes every order, groups the losses by cause and ranks the three fixes worth the most, explained in your language.
landing.step3Text: Accept a fix in one click: it is saved with a 30-day test, a stop rule and the numbers it was based on.
landing.faqChatgptA: ChatGPT gives you a story once; Profyn gives you a ledger every month. A chat model guesses figures and cannot reconcile thousands of orders to channel and product totals. In Profyn a tested engine computes every rupee, the AI only explains them, and any AI sentence with a figure the engine did not produce is rejected.
landing.faqConnectQ: Do I need to connect my store?
landing.faqConnectA: No. Upload the reports you already have: Shopify, Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Razorpay or Shiprocket exports are mapped automatically, and any other CSV is mapped once with AI help. Shopify stores can also connect directly with a read-only access token; Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra connectors are on the roadmap.
landing.faqFilesA: CSV or JSON with a downloadable template and aliases for common column names. Upload up to 12 files at once, for example one per month; they are merged, and orders already saved to your account are skipped.
landing.faqContributionA: It measures what each order leaves after refunds, recovery, shipping, fees and ads. Rent, salaries and tax are not in an order file, so this is operational contribution, not statutory net profit.
landing.faqSafeA: Your data is stored in India (AWS Mumbai), and other accounts cannot read it. The AI sees only totals by cause, never your order rows, and it is off for your uploads unless you switch it on. You can export or delete everything at any time.
landing.faqTrialQ: What is free, and how does the trial work?
landing.faqTrialA: The Free plan covers up to 100 orders a month, with no card. Paid plans start with a 14-day trial on your own orders, with every feature, before you decide anything.

unit.netRevenueFormula: Net revenue = revenue − refunds (revenue is gross sales after discount)
unit.cm1Formula: CM1 = (net revenue − net product cost) ÷ net revenue, where net product cost = product cost − recovered
unit.cm2Formula: CM2 = (net revenue − net product cost − shipping − payment fees − handling) ÷ net revenue; shipping includes return shipping
unit.cm3Formula: CM3 = (net revenue − net product cost − shipping − payment fees − handling − ads) ÷ net revenue; ads are allocated, not caused
unit.netFormula: Net margin = (operational contribution − fixed costs) ÷ net revenue
unit.fixedTip: Assumed: entered by you, kept in this browser, and saved with a decision.

unit.subChannel: Ads are the channel spend, deducted once per channel.
unit.gateClosed: Unknown orders are left out, so these cover computed orders only; the headline margin stays hidden until refund facts are complete.
unit.disclaimer: Estimated operational, not statutory net profit.
unit.fixedSharedTip: Each row carries a share of the fixed costs in proportion to its net revenue (assumed).

definitions.title: How the ledger counts
definitions.netRevenueNote: Revenue is gross sales after discount; the same figure as net sales.
definitions.npc: net product cost = product cost − recovered product cost
definitions.npcNote: Stock that comes back from a return is subtracted once, never twice.
definitions.fee: Deducted separately, on its own line; never folded into shipping or product cost.
definitions.late: A refund dated after the period end is a prior-period adjustment: the period total stays as reported, and the restated total is shown next to it.

aiBadge.ai: AI summary · numbers from the engine

ai.title: Why Profyn, not a chat window
ai.sub: Where AI helps, where it is not allowed to, and the live log that proves it.
ai.quote: ChatGPT gives you a story once; Profyn gives you a ledger every month.
ai.p1Text: Every rupee comes from the same engine on every run, and orders, channels and products add up to the same total. More than {{n}} automated tests guard it, and the public checks run on the reference orders.
ai.p2Text: A {{n}}-order Shopify export was processed end to end, the whole file and not a sample of it.
ai.p3Text: Decisions, assumptions, corrections and their 30-day checks are saved with a date and an owner, so next month starts from what you decided.
ai.p4Text: A refund and its recovery are netted once. Unknown stays unknown, never zero. Refunds dated after the period end are prior-period adjustments, not silent restatements.
ai.p5Text: English, Hindi and Telugu, from import to ledger, leaks, scenario and decision in one place, with a monthly report to share.
ai.p6Text: The AI sees aggregates only: totals, counts and labels. Never order rows, customer names, emails or phone numbers. You can switch it off.
ai.checksLine: Public checks right now: {{passed}} of {{total}} pass.
ai.logSub: Every AI reply is checked against the engine before it is shown: a number the engine did not produce is rejected.
ai.logUnavailable: The guard log is not available on this server yet.
ai.disabled: AI switched off on this server
ai.logNote: Counts since the server started. A rejected reply is replaced by the template text, so the page never shows an unchecked number.
ai.switchSub: Profyn works the same without AI: the explanations use fixed templates instead.
ai.switchAccount: Saved to your account. Off means every explanation uses the template text; the numbers stay the same.
ai.switchGuest: Kept in this browser. Off means every explanation uses the template text; the numbers stay the same.
ai.switchedOff: AI wording is off. Template text only.
ai.defaults: AI wording is off by default for data you upload and on for the synthetic demo.

trust.title: Trust and privacy
trust.sub: The data promise, with what this server reports right now beside each line.
trust.regionHow: Your data is stored in an Indian cloud region.
trust.encPromise: Encrypted at rest and in transit
trust.encHow: HTTPS between your browser and Profyn; the database and file storage are encrypted at rest.
trust.encLocal: This server keeps data in memory only (local run).
trust.ownerHow: Uploads, analyses and decisions belong to your account; other accounts cannot read them. Uploads in the demo go to a shared demo workspace.
trust.aggHow: Totals, counts and labels; never order rows, customer names, emails or phone numbers.
trust.trainHow: Profyn does not train models on your data. AI wording is off by default for uploaded data and on for the synthetic demo.
trust.exportHow: Download everything Profyn holds about you as a file, or delete your account and its data, from your profile.
trust.auditHow: Sign-ins, exports, consent changes and deletions are recorded with a date; you can read your own log.
trust.switchHow: Turn AI wording off; every number stays the same and the explanations use templates.
trust.note: Operational contribution, not statutory profit. The demo uses labelled synthetic data.

flag.discountOverGross: discount_inr is greater than gross_inr on {{id}} — row excluded.
flag.refundOverNet: refund_inr is greater than gross_inr − discount_inr on {{id}} — row excluded.
flag.recoveredOverCost: recovered_product_cost_inr is greater than product_cost_inr on {{id}} — row excluded.

pulse.halveDetail: {{channel}} brings {{n}} orders at {{inr}} contribution; its ads are {{pct}}% of its net sales. Halving ad spend per order there saves about {{save}} if the same orders still come.
pulse.codDetail: COD orders return {{x}}× as often as prepaid. A ₹{{fee}} fee on {{n}} COD orders recovers about {{inr}}, before any shift to prepaid.
pulse.inspectDetail: {{product}} is rank {{units}} on units but {{rank}} on contribution; {{pct}}% of its orders come back. Recovering {{target}}% of product cost on its returns adds about {{inr}}.
pulse.capDetail: Kept orders discounted above {{pct}}% of gross gave away {{inr}} more than a {{cap}}% cap allows, assuming the same orders still happen.
pulse.smallDetail: {{n}} kept orders were under ₹{{limit}}, where shipping takes the most of each rupee. A ₹{{charge}} charge recovers about {{inr}}.
pulse.pushNote: {{product}} sells and earns: rank {{units}} on units, {{rank}} on contribution. Give it more stock and visibility.
pulse.rankNote: {{product}} ranks {{units}} on units but {{rank}} on contribution; {{why}}.
pulse.whyShipping: shipping is {{pct}}% of its order value
pulse.whyPrice: its price leaves little after costs

formula.netRevenue: net revenue = revenue − refunds (gross − discount − refund)
formula.netProductCost: net product cost = product cost − recovered product cost (subtracted once)
formula.cm1: CM1 = (net revenue − net product cost) ÷ net revenue
formula.cm2: CM2 = (net revenue − net product cost − shipping (incl. return shipping) − payment fees − handling) ÷ net revenue
formula.cm3: CM3 = contribution ÷ net revenue = (net revenue − net product cost − shipping (incl. return shipping) − payment fees − handling − ads) ÷ net revenue
formula.netMargin: net margin (estimated) = (contribution − fixed costs) ÷ net revenue; fixed costs are an assumed input, default 0

ai.regionNote: Orders, analyses and decisions are stored in AWS ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Only the aggregate fields listed in fields_sent go to the Gemini API (Google); raw order rows never leave the API. With AI off, every text is the deterministic template.

recon.ok: Σ orders = Σ channels = Σ products
recon.unknown: Channel spend is unknown for at least one channel — totals cannot be reconciled until it is supplied.
recon.gap: Totals differ by {{inr}} — check channel and product assignments.

evidence.noGain: This change does not add money on these orders.
evidence.high: {{n}} orders drive it; in 95% of resamples of your orders it still gains money.
evidence.medium: {{n}} orders drive it; it gains money in {{pct}}% of resamples, so the size is less certain.
evidence.low: Only {{n}} orders drive it, so the result could change with more data.
evidence.missingMany: {{base}} {{n}} orders have missing facts and are left out.
evidence.missingOne: {{base}} {{n}} order with missing facts left out, never counted as zero.
evidence.missingOther: {{base}} {{n}} orders with missing facts left out, never counted as zero.

evidence.tip: Your orders were resampled many times. The fix gained money in {{pct}}% of them, and the change stayed between {{low}} and {{high}} 95% of the time. {{reason}}
